title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: a draft save naming no package of an object its package-less definition owns is judged at its draft address, and refused with a way out to the package-less draft (ADR-0029 D9.9)
body:
Fixes #23712

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What changed

`saveMetaItem`'s ADR-0029 D9.9 object check is now asked of the package the write lands in. A draft save naming no package (`PUT /api/v1/meta/object/NAME?mode=draft`, Studio's designer save) leaves `packageId` empty, and the repository resolves its binding (#11087). Its write lands at `packagelessDraftAddress` (the same rule as `resolveWriteHead` and `unboundItemDraftAddress`). Over active rows `[package-less, Q]` that address is Q's draft, and so is a lone Q draft over `[package-less]`. The check used to ask `classifyObjectContribution(name, null)`, so the `sys_metadata` sentinel owner read `own` and the save answered `200` for a draft no publish can serve; the promote door refuses it since #23514 (PR #23704).

The lane's choice, made by the seat: **refuse before writing**. It answers `422 OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` with nothing written, as the publish-mode save naming no package already is over the same rows.
- `saveMetaItem`, for a draft save naming no package of `type: 'object'` (no `source`, not `package-duplicate`), reads `packagelessDraftAddress` and asks D9.9 of its `into`. An ambiguous address is left to the repository's `409`, unchanged. `request.packageId` is not rewritten: the repository keeps resolving the binding. The draft address itself (`packagelessDraftAddress`, `unboundItemDraftAddress`, `resolveWriteHead`) is untouched.
- `unboundOwnerPackageRefusal` gets one new arm, `mode: 'draft'` + `namedNoPackage`, with a new state field `strandedDrafts`. That field holds the package drafts stored when no draft bound to no package is stored. The arm names, in order, each package row's `DELETE …?package=`, then each such draft's discard `?state=draft&package=`, then "send this save again".
- **H3 measured:** the existing `namedNoPackage` text ("Delete the 'Q' row first … then send this save again") is false for a draft save over Q's draft. Deleting Q's row leaves Q's draft, and the address then still names it, which is H2's cell. So the draft cell gets its own arm, as `adoptedDraft` did at the promote door.

The text, for `[package-less, Q]` with Q's draft (the longest arm with one draft):

> A draft save naming no package of object 'NAME' writes a draft bound to 'Q', which no publish can serve: the object is served by its package-less definition. First DELETE /api/v1/meta/object/NAME?package=Q, then ?state=draft&package=Q (the draft discard), then send this save again: it writes the package-less draft. Nothing was written.

## The narrowing, FROM → TO per cell

Every TO is `422 OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH`, `packageId: Q`, `ownerPackageId: null`, nothing written. `NAME` is owned by its package-less definition; `Q` and `P` are any packages.
- active `[package-less, Q]`, no draft: FROM `200` with a new Q draft. TO the refusal naming `DELETE …?package=Q`, then the save.
- active `[package-less, Q]`, the draft bound to no package: FROM `200` with that draft adopted into Q. TO the same text.
- active `[package-less, Q]`, the draft bound to no package and Q's: FROM `200` into Q's draft. TO the same text (once Q's row is gone the address keeps the unbound draft).
- active `[package-less, Q]`, Q's draft: FROM `200` into Q's draft. TO the text naming `DELETE …?package=Q, then ?state=draft&package=Q`, then the save.
- active `[package-less, Q]`, other packages' drafts and no draft bound to no package (`P`, or `P` + `Q`): FROM `200` into Q's draft. TO the text naming Q's row, then each package draft's discard.
- active `[package-less]`, one package's draft alone (`Q`, or `P`): FROM `200` into that draft. TO the text naming that draft's discard, then the save.

Unchanged: a draft save naming no package with no package row and no package draft (the draft bound to no package is written); with the draft bound to no package stored and no package row; over two packages' rows, or two packages' drafts with neither a row nor a draft bound to no package (`409`); every save naming a package; every publish-mode save; the promote doors; code-package-owned objects (the package door answers `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` first, measured with and without the change); every other type.

Then a fresh boot records the stored rows, the registry owner, the served definition (the data plane's and the metadata read's agree in every row) and the records.

Every refused cell's walk ends where its text says. The 8 narrowed cells land the sent draft in the draft bound to no package, with the object still served by its package-less definition and both records kept, across the boot. The unchanged 422 cells' move texts (PR #23704's) walk into Q as before. The longest new text is 416 characters (row 23, one row and two drafts), under the REST door's 500-character bound.

## Mechanism hypotheses (dispatch), as measured

- **H1 holds** on `main` `2906cd8d2e`: rows 13, 15, 17 and 19 answered `200` into Q's draft. Over the draft bound to no package (row 15) the write **adopts** that draft into Q: after the save only `d:Q` is stored.
- **H2 holds:** row 5 (`[pl]` + Q's draft alone) answered `200` into Q's draft. Its text names the discard naming Q, not the move text.
- **H3 holds:** over `[pl, Q]` + Q's draft, `DELETE …?package=Q` answers `200` and leaves `d:Q` stored. The next draft save naming no package is then H2's cell, and is refused again with the discard text. So that cell's text names both steps.
